text:
Casey Mittelstadt is in his second full season in Boston after stops in Buffalo and Colorado, and he has settled into a middle-six role: about 14 and a half minutes a night, ten points in 18 games, a goal or an assist in seven of his last ten.

The 5v5 numbers look terrific on the surface. Boston has 55% of expected goals with him on the ice. But the actual goals have gone in at a much higher rate than the chances suggest, the most on-ice luck of anyone on this list, and he is shooting 20% against a usual range closer to 15%. Some of this month's success will fade.

What should last is the playmaking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season (81st percentile among forwards), and Evolving-Hockey credited him with 1.4 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. He is a passer first, and his ice time has edged up to 15 minutes lately. Watch whether that keeps growing as the shooting comes back to earth.
headline: Mittelstadt is useful, and a little lucky
